teams.heading: Fiji players knelt to shake Michael D Higgins' hand at the Aviva
teams.body: Ahead of tonight's Aviva Stadium meeting, Balls.ie looks back at the 2024 fixture, when Fiji's players knelt one by one to shake President Michael D Higgins' hand before kick-off. Virgin Media pundit Matt Williams, on duty that day, explained the gesture: "This is the respect of the Malenesian people." Higgins attended that game as his last autumn international at the stadium. Fiji arrive without a point from four Nations Championship games.

lead.why: It is the freshest Fiji-focused item not already reported, and it is about the team rather than Ireland.

teams.heading: Maro Itoje warns England against sleepwalking into Japan clash at Twickenham
teams.body: England captain Maro Itoje has warned his side they cannot afford to sleepwalk into Saturday's clash with Japan, insisting they "need to be alive" to whatever Japan throw at them. Itoje, who made his debut under Japan head coach Eddie Jones in 2016, when Jones was England coach, said Japan are "very consistent at getting speed into the game", and that England's answer is to "impose our game". England have never lost to Japan and have scored 50 or more points in each of their last two meetings.

lead.why: It is a fresh England item from the captain before the match, and it is not a repeat of the Ojomoh recall already reported today.

teams.heading: France U20 lose 27-19 to Italy in Parma despite late pressure
teams.body: France U20, captained by Clément Paul, opened their year in Parma by falling 17-0 behind and going down to 13 men by the 21st minute. Tries from Tyreese Robin and Xan Mariluz before the break cut the gap to 22-14, and the side pushed for the final 40 minutes but could not turn that into victory. France U20 coach Cédric Laborde said there was still plenty of work to do, pointing to imprecision and too many infringements.

lead.why: The South Africa items all retell the already-reported 21-19 win, so the U20 result is the strongest genuinely new story on the shortlist.

teams.heading: Stuart McCloskey says he couldn't care less about Ireland's ageing midfield
teams.body: Ulster centre Stuart McCloskey, one of four 30-somethings in a long-running midfield contest, was asked this week about the ageing of Ireland's centres and was unconcerned. "Honestly, I couldn't care less about the succession of what's going on after me," he told reporters in Abbotstown. The worry is a fair one: the XV that beat Argentina 42-12 last weekend averaged 29.2 years, with eight players aged 30 or over.

lead.why: It is the strongest NEW Ireland item in the pack, with a direct player quote that a fan would pass on, and it is not a repeat of the captaincy, debut or Gibson-Park stories already reported.

teams.heading: Italy players and Gonzalo Quesada pose at Genoa shelter for adoption campaign
teams.body: Italy's players joined head coach Gonzalo Quesada at the Monte Contessa municipal shelter in Genoa, posing with some of the animals in its care during the Captain's Run on the eve of Saturday's Nations Championship test against Argentina at Stadio Luigi Ferraris. The visit backed the 'Adopt, don't buy' campaign, alongside Genoa councillor Francesca Ghio and shelter volunteers. The Federazione Italiana Rugby said it sees the national team's presence as a way to give visibility to causes of value to the wider community.

lead.why: It is the only new Italy-side item on the shortlist that has not already been reported, and the rest are either Nicotera quotes already run or non-Italy stories.

teams.heading: Townsend stresses 'individual responsibility' after seven tries conceded to New Zealand
teams.body: Gregor Townsend says Scotland's problems against New Zealand were more about how they let the All Blacks into their 22 than about defence itself. He accepted that players coming offside or not rolling away quickly are part of the defence, but framed them as individual responsibility. Scotland conceded seven tries in the 21-43 defeat, and Townsend noted that the best teams in the world look to score over 50% of the time from those entries.

lead.why: Townsend's defensive post-mortem on the New Zealand loss is a fresh coach angle that is distinct from the already-reported selection news.

teams.heading: Wales change backroom team as a Grand Slam-winning figure leaves the set-up
teams.body: Wales have changed their backroom team, and one of the Grand Slam winners is no longer part of it. Head coach Steve Tandy's side host New Zealand today, going into the match seventh of 12 on the log after four games: two wins, two defeats and a points difference of -35. The most recent result was last weekend's 28-21 win over Japan.

lead.why: It is the only new item in the shortlist that reports a concrete event about Wales themselves, a change to their coaching set-up.

teams.heading: Pablo Matera captains Pumas against Italy with Montoya sidelined by injury
teams.body: The Pumas' leadership passes to Matera with Montoya ruled out, and the captain says the bench sends a message. Six forwards and two backs, he says, means the game will be decided up front, in the set pieces. He describes an experienced pack, with forward Guido Petti and Matera himself having played many matches, and says Pedro Rubiolo has played whenever available for three years. Looking back at the 42-12 defeat to Ireland, he said the first step had been self-criticism.

lead.why: It is the freshest Argentina-side item in the pack: Matera's pre-match comments on captaincy, the injured Montoya and the bench, and his reaction to the Ireland defeat.

teams.heading: Joseph Suaalii returns to midfield at No 13 for Wallabies against Scotland
teams.body: Suaalii, the rugby league convert, switches from the left wing to the centre for Sunday's Nations Championship clash against Scotland at Murrayfield, replacing Isaac Henry. He started last week's defeat to England at Twickenham on the left wing, and now lines up alongside Len Ikitau at No 12, with Harry Potter moving to No 11. The Wallabies are already out of contention for the inaugural Nations Championship final, having lost three of their four matches.

teams.heading: Warner Dearns to co-captain Japan after Hurricanes' Super Rugby title
teams.body: Japan second row Warner Dearns starts Saturday as co-captain. The 6ft 8in lock moved from Hawke's Bay in New Zealand at 14 when his father took a strength and conditioning job at NEC Green Rockets, and recalls: "I said I didn't want to go." He made his Japan debut in November 2021, aged 19, and after a sabbatical season with the Hurricanes he helped Wellington win their first Super Rugby title in a decade.

lead.why: It is the freshest Japan-specific item on the shortlist, a profile of co-captain Warner Dearns, and it sits clear of the England selection and Jones stories already run.

teams.heading: Frank Bunce says Jordie Barrett, Quinn Tupaea not far from Springboks centres
teams.body: Former All Blacks centre Frank Bunce says Jordie Barrett is "in the conversation for being one of the best in the world". Quinn Tupaea, who impressed at 13 late in 2025, has very much nailed down the jersey under New Zealand head coach Dave Rennie. Bunce told Sport Nation the Springboks pair of Damian de Allende and Jesse Kriel are "possibly not quite as good yet", but insists they are not far off. New Zealand have struggled for a settled midfield since Ma'a Nonu and Conrad Smith retired.

lead.why: A fresh pundit verdict on New Zealand's midfield, which the pack ties to Quinn Tupaea's hold on the 13 jersey, beats the older Dearns and Wales pieces.

teams.heading: Pundits and fans want Springboks punished over Rassie Erasmus' front-row switch
teams.body: South Africa head coach Rassie Erasmus switched his entire front row an hour before kick-off, promoting Gerhard Steenekamp, Jan-Hendrik Wessels and Thomas du Toit into the starting XV and moving Ox Nché, Malcolm Marx and Wilco Louw to the bench. Some pundits and supporters believe the Springboks should be punished, with fans demanding World Rugby clarify its rules. Regulation 15.1.2 requires starting XVs and up to eight replacements to be exchanged 48 hours before kick-off, but it is unclear whether named replacements may start.

lead.why: It is the freshest new angle in the pack, a live question of whether South Africa face sanction over the late front-row switch, and it is not a rerun of the defeat coverage.
